_doc: SOURCE-CUSTODY-PII-01 · ACT 4 §C + CORPUS-AUTHORITY-01 — corpus admission declaration. Enforced by lib/corpus/admission.ts. A file enters MAIA's knowledge corpus ONLY when a rule names it, its classification permits corpus membership, AND the rule carries a compatible structured authority basis. Absence of any one means EXCLUSION.
_law: Membership and authority must be DECLARED and CHECKED, never INHERITED from location, naming, publication status, or a free-text assurance.
_state: One individually governed item is now classified and admissible: Elemental Alchemy. The remaining 735 files under data/ain/source remain unclassified_legacy and excluded. Classification continues item/collection by item/collection; no bulk inheritance from the directory.

_classifications.published_knowledge: ADMITS — authored knowledge intended for MAIA to draw on.
_classifications.third_party_published: ADMITS — third-party published text held under an explicit basis.
_classifications.organizational_public: ADMITS — Soullab's own governed public material.
_classifications.unclassified_legacy: EXCLUDES — present in the tree, never classified.
_classifications.operational_human_record: NEVER ADMITS — known to carry human records.

ACT 4 §C: the historical corpus root. Every file here was ingested by directory convention alone, with no classification and no PII exclusion — the defect this declaration closes. Held closed until each collection is classified on its own evidence.

_authority.soullab_owned: May support published_knowledge or organizational_public only with mechanically locatable evidence: an in-file marker actually present in the work, or a record under docs/corpus-authority/ whose declared marker is present.
_authority.public_domain: May support third_party_published only when mechanically locatable evidence governs the work itself—not an image, quotation, phrase, or unrelated source.
_authority.license: May support third_party_published only when mechanically locatable evidence identifies a license that governs the work and permits the intended corpus use.
_authority.permission: May support third_party_published only when a record under docs/corpus-authority/ carries the declared authorization marker; free-text claims are not authority evidence.
